verses.saheeh: The Prophet frowned and turned away
verses.khattab: He frowned and turned ˹his attention˺ away
verses.jalalayn: ﻿He, the Prophet, frowned, glowered with his face, and turned away,
verses.romanUrdu: [The prophet] Tursh-rooh (frowned) hua aur berukhi barti

verses.saheeh: Because there came to him the blind man, [interrupting].
verses.khattab: ˹simply˺ because the blind man came to him ˹interrupting˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿because the blind man came to him: ‘Abd Allāh son of Umm Maktūm, who interrupted him while he was busy with those notables of Quryash whose submission [to God] he was very eager for. The blind man was not aware that he was busy with these and so he called out to him, ‘Teach me of what God has taught you’. However, the Prophet (s) went off to his house. He was then reproached for this with what was revealed in this sūra. Afterwards, whenever he came to him, the Prophet would say to him, ‘Greetings to him on whose account God reproached me!’, and would lay down his cloak for him.
verses.romanUrdu: Is baat par ke woh andha us ke paas aa gaya

verses.saheeh: But what would make you perceive, [O Muhammad], that perhaps he might be purified
verses.khattab: You never know ˹O Prophet˺, perhaps he may be purified
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And how would you know? Perhaps he would cleanse himself (yazzakkā: the original tā’ [of yatazakkā] has been assimilated with the zāy), that is, [perhaps] he would purge himself of sins by what he hears from you,
verses.romanUrdu: Tumhe kya khabar, shayad woh sudhar jaye

verses.saheeh: Or be reminded and the remembrance would benefit him?
verses.khattab: or he may be mindful, benefitting from the reminder
verses.jalalayn: ﻿or be admonished (yadhdhakkar: the original tā’ [of yatadhakkar] has been assimilated with the dhāl) and so the reminder, the admonition heard from you, might benefit him (a variant reading [for tanfa‘uhu] has tanfa‘ahu as the response to the optative statement).
verses.romanUrdu: ya naseehat par dhyaan de aur naseeat karna us ke liye nafea(faiydamand) ho

verses.saheeh: As for he who thinks himself without need,
verses.khattab: As for the one who was indifferent
verses.jalalayn: ﻿But as for the one [who thinks himself] self-sufficient, through wealth,
verses.romanUrdu: Jo shaks be-parwahi baratta hai

verses.saheeh: To him you give attention.
verses.khattab: you gave him your ˹undivided˺ attention
verses.jalalayn: ﻿to him you [do] attend (tasaddā: a variant reading has tassaddā, where the original second tā’ [of tatasaddā] has been assimilated with the sād), [him] you accept and turn your attention to;
verses.romanUrdu: Uski taraf to tum tawajjuh karte ho

verses.indopak: وَمَا عَلَيْكَ اَ لَّا يَزَّ كّٰى ۗ
verses.saheeh: And not upon you [is any blame] if he will not be purified.
verses.khattab: even though you are not to blame if he would not be purified
verses.jalalayn: ﻿yet it is not your concern if he does not cleanse himself, [if he does not] believe.
verses.romanUrdu: Halaanke agar wo na sudhrey to tum par uski kya zimmedari hai

verses.saheeh: But as for he who came to you striving [for knowledge]
verses.khattab: But as for the one who came to you, eager ˹to learn˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿But as for him who comes to you hurrying (yas‘ā is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of [the verb] jā’a, ‘comes’)
verses.romanUrdu: Aur jo khud tumharey paas dauda aata hai

verses.saheeh: While he fears [Allah],
verses.khattab: being in awe ˹of Allah˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿fearful, of God (wa-huwa yakhshā is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of [the verb] yas‘ā, ‘hurrying’) — this being the blind man —
verses.romanUrdu: Aur woh darr raha hota hai

verses.saheeh: From him you are distracted.
verses.khattab: you were inattentive to him
verses.jalalayn: ﻿to him you pay no heed (talahhā: the original second tā’ [of tatalahhā] has been omitted), that is to say, from him you are distracted [by other things].
verses.romanUrdu: Usse tum berukhi barat-tey ho

verses.saheeh: No! Indeed, these verses are a reminder;
verses.khattab: But no! This ˹revelation˺ is truly a reminder
verses.jalalayn: ﻿No indeed!, do not behave like this. Truly it, the sūra, is, or the verses [are], a reminder, an admonition for [all] creatures —
verses.romanUrdu: Hargiz nahin yeh to ek naseehat hai

verses.saheeh: So whoever wills may remember it.
verses.khattab: So let whoever wills be mindful of it
verses.jalalayn: ﻿so let whoever will, remember it, preserve it [in his memory] and thus be admonished by it —
verses.romanUrdu: jiska jee chahey isey qabool karey

verses.saheeh: [It is recorded] in honored sheets,
verses.khattab: It is ˹written˺ on pages held in honour—
verses.jalalayn: ﻿on leaves (fī suhufin is the second predicate of innahā, ‘truly it’, and what precedes it is a parenthetical statement) [that are] honoured, by God,
verses.romanUrdu: Yeh aisey saheefon mein darj hai jo mukarram hain

verses.saheeh: Exalted and purified,
verses.khattab: highly esteemed, purified—
verses.jalalayn: ﻿elevated, in the heavens, purified, exalted above the touch of devils,
verses.romanUrdu: Buland martaba hain, pakeeza hain

verses.saheeh: [Carried] by the hands of messenger-angels,
verses.khattab: by the hands of angel-scribes
verses.jalalayn: ﻿in the hands of scribes, who write it down from the Preserved Tablet,
verses.romanUrdu: muazzaz aur neik kaatibon ke

verses.saheeh: Noble and dutiful.
verses.khattab: honourable and virtuous
verses.jalalayn: ﻿noble, pious, obedient to God, exalted be He: these being the angels.
verses.romanUrdu: haathon mein rehete hain

verses.saheeh: Cursed is man; how disbelieving is he.
verses.khattab: Condemned are ˹disbelieving˺ humans! How ungrateful they are ˹to Allah˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Perish man!, accursed be the disbeliever! What has made him ungrateful? (an interrogative statement meant as a rebuke) — what has driven him to disbelief?
verses.romanUrdu: Laanat ho Insan par kaisa sakht munkir-e-haq (denies the Truth) hai yeh

verses.saheeh: From what substance did He create him?
verses.khattab: From what substance did He create them
verses.jalalayn: ﻿From what thing has He created him? (an interrogative meant as an affirmative, which He then explains by saying):
verses.romanUrdu: Kis cheez se Allah ne isey paida kiya hai

verses.saheeh: From a sperm-drop He created him and destined for him;
verses.khattab: He created them from a sperm-drop, and ordained their development
verses.jalalayn: ﻿From a drop of sperm did He create him then proportion him, [in stages] as a blood-clot, then an embryo up to the last [stage] of his creation.
verses.romanUrdu: Nutfa ki ek boondh se Allah ne isey paida kiya phir iski taqdeer muqarrar ki

verses.saheeh: Then He eased the way for him;
verses.khattab: Then He makes the way easy for them
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Then He made the way, his exit from his mother’s belly, easy for him;
verses.romanUrdu: Phir iske liye zindagi ki raah aasan ki

verses.saheeh: Then He causes his death and provides a grave for him.
verses.khattab: then causes them to die and be buried
verses.jalalayn: ﻿then He makes him die and buries him, He places him in a grave that hides him;

wbw.translation: and provides a grave for him,

verses.romanUrdu: Phir isey maut di aur qabr mei pahunchaya

verses.saheeh: Then when He wills, He will resurrect him.
verses.khattab: Then when He wills, He will resurrect them
verses.jalalayn: ﻿then, when He wills, He will raise him, for the Resurrection.
verses.romanUrdu: Phir jab chahey woh isey dobara utha khada karey

verses.saheeh: No! Man has not yet accomplished what He commanded him.
verses.khattab: But no! They have failed to comply with what He ordered
verses.jalalayn: ﻿No indeed! Verily, he has not accomplished, he has not done, what He, his Lord, commanded him, to [do].
verses.romanUrdu: Hargiz nahi, isney woh farz ada nahi kiya jiska Allah ne isey hukum diya tha

verses.saheeh: Then let mankind look at his food -
verses.khattab: Let people then consider their food
verses.jalalayn: ﻿So let man consider, in reflection, his [source of] food, how it is determined and procured for him:
verses.romanUrdu: Phir zara insaan apni khuraak(khane/food) ko dekhe

verses.saheeh: How We poured down water in torrents,
verses.khattab: how We pour down rain in abundance
verses.jalalayn: ﻿that We pour down water, from the clouds, plenteously;
verses.romanUrdu: Humne khoob paani lundhaya(poured)

verses.saheeh: Then We broke open the earth, splitting [it with sprouts],
verses.khattab: and meticulously split the earth open ˹for sprouts˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿then We split the earth into fissures, with vegetation,
verses.romanUrdu: Phir zameen ko ajeeb tarah phada

verses.saheeh: And caused to grow within it grain
verses.khattab: causing grain to grow in it
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and cause the grains, such as wheat and barley, to grow therein,
verses.romanUrdu: phir us ke andar ugaye galley(grain)

verses.saheeh: And grapes and herbage
verses.khattab: as well as grapes and greens
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and vines and herbs (qadb is moist qatt),
verses.romanUrdu: Aur angoor aur tarkariyan

verses.saheeh: And olive and palm trees
verses.khattab: and olives and palm trees
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and olives and date-palms,
verses.romanUrdu: Aur zaitoon aur khajoorein

verses.saheeh: And gardens of dense shrubbery
verses.khattab: and dense orchards
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and gardens of dense foliage, orchards teeming with trees,
verses.romanUrdu: Aur ghaney baagh(orchards)

verses.saheeh: And fruit and grass -
verses.khattab: and fruit and fodder—
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and fruits and pastures (abb is what cattle graze; it is also said to be ‘straw’),
verses.romanUrdu: Aur tarah tarah ke phal aur chaarey

verses.saheeh: [As] enjoyment for you and your grazing livestock.
verses.khattab: all as ˹a means of˺ sustenance for you and your animals
verses.jalalayn: ﻿as sustenance (understand matā‘an as mut‘atan or tamtī‘an, as explained above in the previous sūra) for you and your flocks (also as [explained] above).
verses.romanUrdu: Tumharey liye aur tumharey maweshion(cattles) ke liye saman-e-zeist(provision )ke taur par

verses.saheeh: But when there comes the Deafening Blast
verses.khattab: Then, when the Deafening Blast comes to pass—
verses.jalalayn: ﻿So when the [deafening] Cry, the second blast, comes —
verses.romanUrdu: Aakhir-e-kaar jab woh kaan behrey kar deney wali aawaz buland hogi

verses.saheeh: On the Day a man will flee from his brother
verses.khattab: on that Day every person will flee from their own siblings
verses.jalalayn: ﻿the day when a man will flee from his [own] brother,
verses.romanUrdu: Us roz aadmi apne bhai

verses.saheeh: And his mother and his father
verses.khattab: and ˹even˺ their mother and father
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and his mother and his father,
verses.romanUrdu: Aur apni maa aur apne baap

verses.saheeh: And his wife and his children,
verses.khattab: and ˹even˺ their spouse and children
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and his wife and his sons (yawma, ‘the day [when]’, is a substitution for idhā, ‘when’, the response to which is indicated by [what follows]) —
verses.romanUrdu: Aur apni biwi aur apni aulad se bhagega

verses.uthmani: لِكُلِّ ٱمۡرِيٕٖ مِّنۡهُمۡ يَوۡمَئِذٖ شَأۡنٞ يُغۡنِيهِ
verses.indopak: لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مِّنْهُمْ يَوْمَٮِٕذٍ شَأْنٌ يُّغْنِيْهِ ۗ
verses.transliteration: likulli imriin minhum yawmaithin shanun yughneehi
verses.saheeh: For every man, that Day, will be a matter adequate for him.
verses.khattab: For then everyone will have enough concern of their own
verses.jalalayn: ﻿every person that day will have a matter to preoccupy him, a predicament to distract him from the affairs of others, in other words, every person will be preoccupied with his own self.
verses.romanUrdu: Unmein har shaks par us din aisa waqt aa padega ke usay apne siwa kisi ka hosh na hoga

verses.saheeh: [Some] faces, that Day, will be bright -
verses.khattab: On that Day ˹some˺ faces will be bright
verses.jalalayn: ﻿On that day some faces will be shining, radiant,
verses.romanUrdu: Kuch chehrey us roz damak rahe hongey

verses.saheeh: Laughing, rejoicing at good news.
verses.khattab: laughing and rejoicing
verses.jalalayn: ﻿laughing, joyous, happy — these are the believers.
verses.romanUrdu: Hashash bashash aur khush o khurram hongey

verses.saheeh: And [other] faces, that Day, will have upon them dust.
verses.khattab: while ˹other˺ faces will be dusty
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And some faces on that day will be covered with dust,
verses.romanUrdu: Aur kuch chehron par uss roz khaak(dust) udd rahi hogi

verses.saheeh: Blackness will cover them.
verses.khattab: cast in gloom—
verses.jalalayn: ﻿overcast, covered, with gloom, darkness and blackness.
verses.romanUrdu: Aur kalons(darkness) chayi hui hogi

verses.saheeh: Those are the disbelievers, the wicked ones.
verses.khattab: those are the disbelievers, the ˹wicked˺ sinners
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Those, the people of this predicament, are the disbelievers, the profligates, those who have combined disbelief with profligacy.
verses.romanUrdu: Yahi kafir o fajir (unbelivers and wicked) log hain
